title: Personal Portfolio Page
description: Build a fully responsive, accessible personal portfolio to showcase your skills and projects.
problemStatement:
You are a front‑end developer looking to land your first client. You need a personal portfolio that demonstrates your HTML and CSS skills.

**Objective:** Create a one‑page portfolio site that works beautifully on mobile, tablet, and desktop.

**Sections to include:**
1. **Header & Navigation** – Your name/logo and internal links to other sections (About, Projects, Contact). The navigation must collapse into a hamburger menu on mobile.
2. **Hero** – A short introduction with your name, tagline, and a call‑to‑action button that scrolls to the Projects section.
3. **About Me** – A short bio, possibly with a profile picture (use a placeholder image or an emoji). Use semantic tags.
4. **Projects** – A grid of 4‑6 project cards. Each card should have an image placeholder, a title, a short description, and a link (even if href="#"). On mobile, cards stack in one column; on tablet, two columns; on desktop, three.
5. **Contact** – A form with fields for name, email, subject (dropdown: General Inquiry, Collaboration, Other), and message. Include labels, validation (required fields), and a submit button.
6. **Footer** – Social links (just icons or text) and copyright.

**Technical Requirements:**
- Semantic HTML5 throughout (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<footer>`).
- Mobile‑first CSS with at least two breakpoints (600px and 900px).
- Use CSS Grid or Flexbox (or both) for layout.
- Use CSS custom properties (variables) for colours and spacing.
- Smooth scroll behaviour when clicking anchor links.
- A visible `:focus` style for keyboard users.
- Accessible hamburger menu: button with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`.
- Responsive images using `srcset` (or at least `max-width: 100%`) and proper `alt` text.
- Form must have accessible labels (explicit for/id).
- Add a 'skip to main content' link.

**Deliverable:** A single HTML file with internal CSS (or a link to an external CSS if you prefer, but for this project internal is fine).
requirements: Mobile‑first responsive design with at least two breakpoints
Accessible navigation (hamburger menu with ARIA, skip link)
Project cards grid using CSS Grid or Flexbox
Contact form with labels, required fields, and a submit button
CSS custom properties for theme colours
hints: For the hamburger menu, you can use a CSS‑only approach with a hidden checkbox, or add a small JavaScript snippet to toggle a class. The CSS should style the menu as open when the class is present.
Use `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr));` for the project cards grid to make it responsive without breakpoints.
For smooth scrolling, use `scroll-behavior: smooth;` on the `html` element.
The skip link CSS: `.skip-link { position: absolute; top: -40px; left: 0; } .skip-link:focus { top: 0; }`
expectedOutput: A responsive portfolio page that passes basic accessibility checks (Lighthouse ≥ 90), renders correctly on mobile/tablet/desktop, and includes all specified sections.
